from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Colors
        V_COLOR = "#00FF00"  # Green
        V2_COLOR = "#FFFF00" # Yellow
        W_COLOR = "#0000FF"  # Blue
        SUM_COLOR = "#FF00FF" # Magenta

        self.setup_layout(
            "Prerequisite: Vectors as Movements", 
            [
                'Vectors are instructions for moving through space.', 
                'We scale vectors to stretch or shrink their movement.', 
                'Adding vectors means following one movement after another.'
            ]
        )
        
        # Grid/Coordinate system background (Visual only)
        # Using a small NumberPlane placed in the grid area
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[0, 6, 1],
            y_range=[0, 6, 1],
            x_length=5,
            y_length=5,
            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.4},
            axis_config={"include_tip": True}
        )
        self.place_in_area(plane, 'A1', 'F6')
        self.add(plane)

        # Vector origin point in the grid space
        # We'll use local coordinates relative to the plane's origin
        origin = plane.c2p(1, 1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(V_COLOR))
        
        # Vector v: (1,1) to (3,2) on plane (length 2, 1)
        v_arrow = Arrow(
            start=origin,
            end=plane.c2p(3, 2),
            buff=0,
            color=V_COLOR,
            stroke_width=6
        )
        v_label = Text("v", font_size=24, color=V_COLOR)
        # Position label near tip (approximate using plane coords)
        v_label.move_to(plane.c2p(3.2, 2.2))
        
        self.play(GrowArrow(v_arrow), FadeIn(v_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(V2_COLOR)
        )
        
        # Vector 2v: (1,1) to (5,3) on plane (length 4, 2)
        v2_arrow = Arrow(
            start=origin,
            end=plane.c2p(5, 3),
            buff=0,
            color=V2_COLOR,
            stroke_width=6
        )
        v2_label = Text("2v", font_size=24, color=V2_COLOR)
        v2_label.move_to(plane.c2p(5.2, 3.2))
        
        self.play(
            Transform(v_arrow, v2_arrow),
            Transform(v_label, v2_label)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(W_COLOR)
        )
        
        # Vector w: (1,1) to (2, -0.5) movement
        # First show w at origin
        w_start_pos = origin
        w_end_pos = plane.c2p(2, 0.5) # instruction is (1, -0.5)
        w_arrow = Arrow(
            start=w_start_pos,
            end=w_end_pos,
            buff=0,
            color=W_COLOR,
            stroke_width=6
        )
        w_label = Text("w", font_size=24, color=W_COLOR)
        w_label.move_to(plane.c2p(2.2, 0.7))
        
        self.play(GrowArrow(w_arrow), FadeIn(w_label))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Move w to the tip of 2v
        # 2v tip is plane.c2p(5, 3)
        # new w end is tip + (1, -0.5) = (6, 2.5)
        new_w_start = plane.c2p(5, 3)
        new_w_end = plane.c2p(6, 2.5)
        
        self.play(
            w_arrow.animate.move_to((new_w_start + new_w_end) / 2).rotate(0), # Dummy to trigger animate
            w_label.animate.move_to(plane.c2p(6.2, 2.7))
        )
        # Using a direct move for accuracy since rotation might be weird with move_to center
        self.play(
            w_arrow.animate.shift(new_w_start - origin)
        )
        
        # Final Sum Vector
        sum_arrow = Arrow(
            start=origin,
            end=new_w_end,
            buff=0,
            color=SUM_COLOR,
            stroke_width=8
        )
        sum_label = Text("2v + w", font_size=24, color=SUM_COLOR)
        sum_label.move_to(plane.c2p(3.5, 1.5))
        
        self.play(GrowArrow(sum_arrow), FadeIn(sum_label))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout with specific title and lecture lines
        lecture_lines = [
            'Combine scaling and addition to reach new locations.',
            'The formula a v + b w represents a linear combination.',
            'Think of vectors as ingredients for a specific recipe.',
            'Adjusting the scalars a and b moves the point.',
            'Every reachable point is a mix of these vectors.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Linear Combinations: Mixing the Ingredients", lecture_lines)

        # Vector Definitions
        # We define them relative to the plane's origin
        v_coords = np.array([1.5, 0.5, 0])
        w_coords = np.array([0.5, 1.5, 0])
        
        # Setup Coordinate Plane on the right
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-1, 4, 1],
            y_range=[-1, 4, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=4,
            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.4}
        )
        self.place_in_area(plane, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.9)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        v_vec = Arrow(plane.c2p(0,0,0), plane.c2p(*v_coords), buff=0, color="#00FF00")
        w_vec = Arrow(plane.c2p(0,0,0), plane.c2p(*w_coords), buff=0, color="#0000FF")
        v_label = Text("v", color="#00FF00", font_size=20)
        w_label = Text("w", color="#0000FF", font_size=20)
        
        # Positioning labels near vector tips
        v_label.next_to(v_vec.get_end(), RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        w_label.next_to(w_vec.get_end(), UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(plane))
        self.play(GrowArrow(v_vec), GrowArrow(w_vec), FadeIn(v_label), FadeIn(w_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        formula = Text("a v + b w", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'A3', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        recipe_label = Text("Vector Recipe", font_size=18, color=GRAY)
        recipe_label.next_to(formula, DOWN, buff=0.2)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(recipe_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Scale v by 0.5 and w by 1.5
        v_scaled_coords = v_coords * 0.5
        w_scaled_coords = w_coords * 1.5
        
        v_scaled_vec = Arrow(plane.c2p(0,0,0), plane.c2p(*v_scaled_coords), buff=0, color="#00FF00")
        w_scaled_vec = Arrow(plane.c2p(0,0,0), plane.c2p(*w_scaled_coords), buff=0, color="#0000FF")
        
        # Dashed lines for the scaled components
        dash_v = DashedLine(plane.c2p(0,0,0), plane.c2p(*v_scaled_coords), color="#00FF00", stroke_opacity=0.6)
        dash_w = DashedLine(plane.c2p(0,0,0), plane.c2p(*w_scaled_coords), color="#0000FF", stroke_opacity=0.6)

        # Update labels to include scalars
        v_scalar_label = Text("0.5v", color="#00FF00", font_size=18)
        w_scalar_label = Text("1.5w", color="#0000FF", font_size=18)
        v_scalar_label.next_to(v_scaled_vec.get_end(), DOWN, buff=0.1)
        w_scalar_label.next_to(w_scaled_vec.get_end(), LEFT, buff=0.1)

        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(v_vec, v_scaled_vec),
            ReplacementTransform(w_vec, w_scaled_vec),
            ReplacementTransform(v_label, v_scalar_label),
            ReplacementTransform(w_label, w_scalar_label),
            FadeIn(dash_v),
            FadeIn(dash_w)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FF00FF") # Matching the resulting vector color
        
        # Parallelogram rule
        res_coords = v_scaled_coords + w_scaled_coords
        
        # Add side lines for parallelogram
        side1 = DashedLine(plane.c2p(*v_scaled_coords), plane.c2p(*res_coords), color=WHITE, stroke_opacity=0.5)
        side2 = DashedLine(plane.c2p(*w_scaled_coords), plane.c2p(*res_coords), color=WHITE, stroke_opacity=0.5)
        
        res_vec = Arrow(plane.c2p(0,0,0), plane.c2p(*res_coords), buff=0, color="#FF00FF")
        res_label = Text("0.5v + 1.5w", color="#FF00FF", font_size=20)
        res_label.next_to(res_vec.get_end(), UR, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(side1), Create(side2))
        self.play(GrowArrow(res_vec), FadeIn(res_label))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            'The span is the collection of all reachable points.', 
            'Two non-parallel vectors span an entire 2D plane.', 
            'If vectors are parallel, their span collapses to a line.', 
            'Adding more directions can expand the reachable universe.', 
            'Span defines the dimensionality of the subspace.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Span: The Reachable Universe", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define origin for the vector operations on the right side
        # Intersection of D-E rows and 3-4 columns
        origin = self.grid["D4"]
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        v1_vec = np.array([1.2, 0.4, 0])
        v2_vec = np.array([0.4, 1.2, 0])
        
        v1 = Arrow(start=origin, end=origin + v1_vec, color="#00FF00", buff=0, stroke_width=6)
        v2 = Arrow(start=origin, end=origin + v2_vec, color="#0000FF", buff=0, stroke_width=6)
        
        v1_label = Text("v1", font_size=20, color="#00FF00")
        v2_label = Text("v2", font_size=20, color="#0000FF")
        
        v1_label.move_to(origin + v1_vec + [0.4, 0.2, 0])
        v2_label.move_to(origin + v2_vec + [0.2, 0.4, 0])

        self.play(GrowArrow(v1), Write(v1_label))
        self.play(GrowArrow(v2), Write(v2_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Shaded background and grid
        plane_rect = Rectangle(width=5.5, height=5.5, fill_color="#222222", fill_opacity=0.7, stroke_width=0)
        self.place_in_area(plane_rect, "A1", "F6")
        
        grid_lines = VGroup()
        for i in range(-5, 6):
            l1 = Line(origin + i*0.4*v1_vec - 2.5*v2_vec, origin + i*0.4*v1_vec + 2.5*v2_vec, color="#444444", stroke_width=1)
            l2 = Line(origin + i*0.4*v2_vec - 2.5*v1_vec, origin + i*0.4*v2_vec + 2.5*v1_vec, color="#444444", stroke_width=1)
            grid_lines.add(l1, l2)
            
        span_tag = Text("Span", font_size=28, color=WHITE).set_opacity(0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(span_tag, "B5")

        self.play(FadeIn(plane_rect), Create(grid_lines), Write(span_tag))
        
        # Linear combinations (points) appearing
        dots = VGroup()
        point_coeffs = [(1.5, 0.5), (-0.8, 1.2), (0.2, -1.5), (-1.2, -0.8), (0.8, 0.8)]
        for c1, c2 in point_coeffs:
            dot = Dot(origin + c1*v1_vec + c2*v2_vec, color=WHITE, radius=0.06)
            dots.add(dot)
            
        self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(d) for d in dots], lag_ratio=0.2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Transform v2 to overlap v1 direction
        v2_parallel_vec = v1_vec * 0.7
        v2_target_arrow = Arrow(start=origin, end=origin + v2_parallel_vec, color="#0000FF", buff=0, stroke_width=6)
        
        # Plane collapses to a line
        collapsed_line = Line(origin - 2.5*v1_vec, origin + 2.5*v1_vec, color="#FFFF00", stroke_width=8)
        
        self.play(
            Transform(v2, v2_target_arrow),
            v2_label.animate.move_to(origin + v2_parallel_vec + [0.1, -0.4, 0]),
            Transform(plane_rect, collapsed_line),
            FadeOut(grid_lines),
            FadeOut(dots),
            span_tag.animate.set_color("#FFFF00").move_to(self.grid["C6"])
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # New vector v3 in a different direction
        v3_vec = np.array([-1.2, 1.0, 0])
        v3 = Arrow(start=origin, end=origin + v3_vec, color="#FF00FF", buff=0, stroke_width=6)
        v3_label = Text("v3", font_size=20, color="#FF00FF")
        v3_label.move_to(origin + v3_vec + [-0.4, 0.2, 0])
        
        # Restore plane visualization
        new_plane = Rectangle(width=5.5, height=5.5, fill_color="#222222", fill_opacity=0.7, stroke_width=0)
        self.place_in_area(new_plane, "A1", "F6")

        self.play(GrowArrow(v3), Write(v3_label))
        self.play(
            Transform(plane_rect, new_plane),
            span_tag.animate.set_color(WHITE).move_to(self.grid["B5"])
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        dim_info = Text("Dimension = 2", font_size=22, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(dim_info, "F4")
        
        self.play(Write(dim_info))
        self.play(Indicate(dim_info, color=YELLOW), Flash(origin, color=WHITE))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            'A set is linearly dependent if it contains redundancy.',
            'Redundant vectors can be built from the others.',
            'Linearly independent vectors each provide a unique direction.',
            'Three vectors in 2D space are always linearly dependent.',
            'Independence ensures every vector adds value to the span.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Linear Dependence: The Redundant Helper", lecture_lines)

        # Vector colors
        V1_COLOR = "#00FF00" # Green
        V2_COLOR = "#0000FF" # Blue
        V3_COLOR = "#FFFF00" # Yellow
        DEPENDENT_COLOR = "#FF0000" # Red
        SPAN_COLOR = "#222222" # Dark Grey

        # Origin for vectors
        origin = self.grid["D3"]

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Define v1 and v2
        v1_end = self.grid["C2"]
        v2_end = self.grid["E2"]
        v1 = Arrow(origin, v1_end, buff=0, color=V1_COLOR)
        v2 = Arrow(origin, v2_end, buff=0, color=V2_COLOR)
        
        v1_label = Text("v1", font_size=18, color=V1_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(v1_label, "C1")
        v2_label = Text("v2", font_size=18, color=V2_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(v2_label, "E1")

        # Shaded span (covering the background of the grid area)
        span_poly = Polygon(
            self.grid["A1"], self.grid["A6"], self.grid["F6"], self.grid["F1"],
            fill_color=SPAN_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.5, stroke_width=0
        )
        
        self.play(FadeIn(span_poly))
        self.play(GrowArrow(v1), GrowArrow(v2))
        self.play(Write(v1_label), Write(v2_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # v3 points to the sum of v1 and v2 (vector addition logic)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(YELLOW))

import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        label_k = Text("k", font_size=18, color="#0000FF")
        self.place_at_grid(label_k, "C4", scale_factor=1.0).shift(LEFT*0.3 + DOWN*0.3)

        # Show k = i + j (redundancy)
        ghost_i = vec_i.copy().set_stroke(opacity=0.5)
        ghost_j = vec_j.copy().set_stroke(opacity=0.5).shift(RIGHT)
        
        self.play(GrowArrow(vec_k), FadeIn(label_k))

        # Visual proof of dependence
        self.play(

        cross_mark = Text("X", color=RED, font_size=40).move_to(vec_k.get_center())
        
        self.play(FadeIn(cross_mark))
        self.wait(2)

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialize the layout
        lecture_lines = [
            "Linear combinations create span through independent basis vectors.",
            "A basis is the ultimate toolkit for vector spaces.",
            "Mastering these concepts unlocks the power of linear algebra."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Synthesis", lecture_lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Line color matches summary text
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        
        word_span = Text("Span", color="#FFFFFF")
        word_ind = Text("Independence", color="#FFFFFF")
        word_basis = Text("Basis", color="#FFFFFF")
        
        # Position words in a column on the right
        self.place_at_grid(word_span, "B4", scale_factor=0.9)
        self.place_at_grid(word_ind, "C4", scale_factor=0.9)
        self.place_at_grid(word_basis, "D4", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        summary_group = VGroup(word_span, word_ind, word_basis)
        self.play(Write(summary_group))
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Line color matches the primary basis vector
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FF00"),
            FadeOut(summary_group)
        )
        
        # Visualizing a basis generating a span (grid)
        # Choose a central origin on the right grid
        origin_point = self.grid["D4"]
        
        # Define basis vectors
        v1_vec = np.array([1.2, 0, 0])
        v2_vec = np.array([0.4, 0.8, 0])
        
        v1 = Arrow(start=origin_point, end=origin_point + v1_vec, color="#00FF00", buff=0)
        v2 = Arrow(start=origin_point, end=origin_point + v2_vec, color="#0000FF", buff=0)
        
        # Generate a parallelogram grid
        grid_lines = VGroup()
        # Lines parallel to v2
        for i in range(-3, 4):
            line_start = origin_point + i * v1_vec - 2 * v2_vec
            line_end = origin_point + i * v1_vec + 2 * v2_vec
            grid_lines.add(Line(line_start, line_end, color=GREY, stroke_opacity=0.4))
        
        # Lines parallel to v1
        for j in range(-2, 3):
            line_start = origin_point + j * v2_vec - 3 * v1_vec
            line_end = origin_point + j * v2_vec + 3 * v1_vec
            grid_lines.add(Line(line_start, line_end, color=GREY, stroke_opacity=0.4))

        self.play(GrowArrow(v1), GrowArrow(v2))
        self.play(Create(grid_lines, run_time=2))
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Line color matches final title
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"),
            FadeOut(grid_lines),
            FadeOut(v1),
            FadeOut(v2)
        )
        
        final_title = Text("The DNA of Vector Spaces", color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_in_area(final_title, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(Write(final_title))
        # Pulse effect: scale up and down
        self.play(
            final_title.animate.scale(1.15),
            rate_func=there_and_back,
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The DNA of Vector Spaces: Span, Linear Dependence, and Bases

sections.title: Prerequisite: Vectors as Movements
sections.content: Briefly recap vectors not just as coordinates, but as 'instructions for movement.' Introduce scalar multiplication (stretching/shrinking) and vector addition (following one instruction after another). Visual: A point starting at the origin, moving along an arrow $\vec{v}$.
sections.example: A delivery drone is told to move 2 units East ($\vec{i}$) and 3 units North ($\vec{j}$). The final position is the vector $2\vec{i} + 3\vec{j}$.

sections.title: Linear Combinations: Mixing the Ingredients
sections.content: Define a linear combination as the result of scaling and adding a set of vectors. Explain the formula $a\vec{v} + b\vec{w}$. Visual: Two vectors $\vec{v}$ and $\vec{w}$ on a grid. Show various points reachable by changing the 'knobs' of scalars $a$ and $b$.
sections.example: An artist mixes blue paint (vector $\vec{B}$) and yellow paint (vector $\vec{Y}$) in different proportions to create various shades of green. Each shade is a linear combination of $\vec{B}$ and $\vec{Y}$.

sections.title: Span: The Reachable Universe
sections.content: The 'Span' is the set of all possible linear combinations of a group of vectors. Visually demonstrate that two non-parallel vectors in 3D space span a flat 2D plane. If they are parallel, they only span a 1D line.
sections.example: A 'Spider-Bot' can only move along two non-parallel silk threads. The entire flat web surface that the bot can traverse is the 'Span' of those two thread vectors.

sections.title: Linear Dependence: The Redundant Helper
sections.content: Introduce linear dependence as 'redundancy.' If one vector can be created by a linear combination of others, it adds nothing to the span. Linear independence means every vector provides a unique direction. Visual: Three arrows in 2D. Show that the 3rd arrow can be built using the first two, making it 'linearly dependent.'
sections.example: A navigation system has three directions: North, East, and North-East. The 'North-East' instruction is redundant (linearly dependent) because you can achieve it by combining North and East.

sections.title: The Basis: The Efficient Blueprint
sections.content: A Basis is the 'Goldilocks' set of vectors: It must span the entire space AND be linearly independent (no redundancy). It is the minimum number of vectors needed to reach every point in the space. Visual: A 3D coordinate system where the x, y, and z axes are highlighted as the standard basis.
sections.example: In a 3D building, you need exactly three directions (Length, Width, Height) to pinpoint any room. Two is not enough (won't span the space); four is too many (one will be dependent). These three 'perfect' instructions form the Basis.

sections.title: Summary & Synthesis
sections.content: Tie all concepts together. Vectors are tools; Linear combinations are how we use them; Span is where they can go; Independence is efficiency; and Basis is the ultimate toolkit. Animation: A grid expanding from two vectors to fill a whole plane.
sections.example: Think of a Basis as the 'Primary Colors' of a vector space. They are independent (you can't make Red from Blue) and they Span the space (you can make any color from them).

storyboard.title: Prerequisite: Vectors as Movements
lecture_lines: Vectors are simple instructions for movement in space.
Scaling a vector stretches or shrinks its path.
Adding vectors combines multiple movements into one.
animations: Draw a vector arrow v from (0,0) to (2,1) in #00FF00; label it 'v' at the tip.
Animate vector v stretching to twice its length, changing color to #FFFF00, labeled '2v'.
Move a new vector w (#0000FF) from origin to the tip of 2v, showing the sum 2v + w.

storyboard.title: Linear Combinations: Mixing the Ingredients
lecture_lines: Start with two distinct movement vectors, v and w.
Scaling both vectors creates new instructions for travel.
Their sum forms a unique linear combination.
animations: Show vectors v (#00FF00) and w (#0000FF) anchored at the origin, incorporating the [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/travel.svg] icon to represent displacement.
Scale v by 0.5 and w by 1.5 simultaneously; show dashed lines for the scaled versions.
Show the parallelogram rule to find the resulting vector #FF00FF, labeled '0.5v + 1.5w'.

storyboard.title: Span: The Reachable Universe
lecture_lines: Take two vectors pointing in different directions.
Together, they generate a grid of possible paths.
Scaling and adding them reaches any point on this grid.
This entire reachable region is called the span.
If parallel, the span collapses to a single line.
animations: Draw two vectors v1 (#00FF00) and v2 (#0000FF) with different directions.
Create a 2D grid (#444444) aligned with v1 and v2 that covers the screen.
Animate several points appearing on the grid as different linear combinations of v1 and v2.
Shade the entire background area covered by the grid in #222222, labeling it 'Span'.
Rotate v2 until it overlaps v1; the #222222 area shrinks to a single line (#FFFF00).

storyboard.title: Linear Dependence: The Redundant Helper
lecture_lines: Imagine two vectors spanning a full flat plane.
Add a third vector already landing within that span.
This third vector is just a mix of others.
We call this redundancy linear dependence.
The reachable span remains exactly the same size.
animations: Start with vectors v1 (#00FF00) and v2 (#0000FF) spanning a plane (shaded #222222).
Introduce a third vector v3 (#FFFF00) pointing to a position already in the #222222 span.
Show ghost copies of v1 and v2 scaled and added to reach the tip of v3.
Highlight v3 in #FF0000 and display the text 'Linearly Dependent' next to it.
Remove v3 and show the shaded span (#222222) remains unchanged, proving redundancy.

storyboard.title: The Basis: The Efficient Blueprint
lecture_lines: Use two independent vectors to build a space.
These vectors span every single point in 2D.
With no redundancy, every vector provides unique direction.
This efficient set is called a basis.
Adding more vectors creates unnecessary linear dependence.
animations: Show two perpendicular vectors i (#FF0000) and j (#00FF00) in 2D space.
Fill the entire screen with a coordinate grid (#444444) based on i and j.
Flash i and j in #FFFFFF to signify they are linearly independent.
Label the pair {i, j} as 'Basis for 2D Space' in #FFFFFF.
Add a third vector k (#0000FF); show it can be formed by i and j, so it's not part of the basis.

storyboard.title: Summary & Synthesis
lecture_lines: Linear combinations and span define our reachable space.
An independent basis provides the most efficient toolkit.
Mastering these foundations unlocks all of linear algebra.
animations: Show a summary screen with the words 'Span', 'Independence', and 'Basis' in #FFFFFF, incorporating the toolkit icon [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/toolkit.svg].
Animate a small set of vectors (#00FF00, #0000FF) generating a full grid.
Display the final title 'The DNA of Vector Spaces' in #FFFF00 with a pulse effect.
